title: Atlee and Priya Welcome Daughter Miyou — And Bollywood's Favourite Director-Dad Era Continues
excerpt: The Jawan director and wife Priya Mohan reveal their newborn daughter's name after keeping fans guessing for a month
body:
# Atlee and Priya Welcome Daughter Miyou — And Bollywood's Favourite Director-Dad Era Continues

The man who gave us Jawan has a new production, and this one doesn't need a box office opening.

Filmmaker Atlee Kumar and wife Priya Mohan — known to fans as Priya Atlee — announced on Instagram today that their newborn daughter's name is Miyou. The name, they shared, means "beauty, gentleness, and love," which is about as far from the explosive, whistle-worthy filmmaking Atlee is known for as you can get. Turns out the director of India's biggest action blockbuster is a total softie at home.

Baby Miyou was actually born on April 20, 2026, but the couple waited nearly a month before sharing the name publicly — a move that, in an era of instant celebrity baby reveals, feels almost countercultural. The announcement came in the form of a pastel-themed Instagram post featuring a tender photo of the baby's hand, accompanied by a specially curated song that Atlee included in the reveal.

Growing the Family

Miyou is the couple's second child. Their first, son Meer, was born on January 31, 2023 — right around the time Atlee was in the thick of post-production on what would become the year's biggest Hindi film. Full name: Miyou Atlee Kumar.

The congratulations poured in almost immediately. Rashmika Mandanna and Samantha Ruth Prabhu were among the Bollywood and South Indian stars who flooded the comments with heart emojis and blessings. The warmth was genuine — Atlee is one of those rare industry figures who seems to be universally liked, the kind of filmmaker who inspires loyalty from both audiences and colleagues.

From Jawan to Raaka

For the uninitiated (and if you're uninitiated, what have you been doing?), Atlee is the 37-year-old Tamil filmmaker who directed Jawan — Shah Rukh Khan's 2023 mega-blockbuster that earned over ₹1,100 crore worldwide and essentially rebooted SRK's career. Before that, he'd already built a formidable reputation in South Indian cinema with Theri, Mersal, and Bigil, all starring Vijay, all massive hits.

Now he's working on Raaka, a pan-Indian fantasy drama that pairs Allu Arjun (yes, the Pushpa man himself) with Deepika Padukone. If that casting doesn't make you sit up straight, check your pulse. Raaka is shaping up to be one of the most anticipated Indian films on the horizon, blending Atlee's mastery of crowd-pleasing spectacle with a fantasy genre that Indian cinema has rarely attempted at this scale.

Why the Diaspora Cares

Atlee became a household name in the Indian diaspora specifically because of Jawan. NRIs will remember the experience vividly — the lines wrapping around AMC theatres in New Jersey, the packed-out Cineplex screenings in Brampton, the collective roar in theatres from Melbourne to Manchester when Shah Rukh Khan appeared in that double role. Jawan wasn't just a film for the diaspora; it was an event, a communal experience that briefly turned every international cinema screening into a festival.

The anticipation for Raaka is already building along similar lines. Allu Arjun's Pushpa franchise ignited its own diaspora frenzy — "Pushpa fever" was as real in Dallas as it was in Delhi. Pairing him with Deepika Padukone under Atlee's direction is the kind of casting that makes diaspora WhatsApp groups explode with speculation months before a single trailer drops.

A Soft Chapter

But today isn't about box office projections or franchise mathematics. Today is about a filmmaker and his wife sharing a quiet, beautiful moment with the world — a new name, a new life, a family growing. The pastel post. The baby's hand. The song.

In an industry that moves at breakneck speed, where the next release date and the next opening weekend dominate every conversation, there's something lovely about Atlee and Priya taking nearly a month to simply be parents before letting the world in.

Welcome, Miyou. Your dad makes the biggest films in India, but something tells us you'll be his greatest production yet.
